variants.title: One client floods the public API
variants.context: A single API key sends 20,000 req/s and the shared cluster’s p99 jumps from 80ms to 4s.
variants.constraint: Other tenants are healthy but share the same edge.
variants.question: What protects the majority of clients?
variants.expectedPattern: Per-key rate limits at the edge so one caller cannot consume the whole fleet.

variants.title: Login brute force
variants.context: Password guesses hit /login from many IPs against one account.
variants.constraint: You must slow attackers without locking out the real user forever.
variants.question: Where should the limit sit?
variants.expectedPattern: Rate-limit by account and IP on the auth path, with backoff rather than a silent 200.
wrongChoices: No limit on login because it is a small JSON body
Store passwords in a cache with no attempt counter

variants.title: Burst vs sustained traffic
variants.context: A mobile app retries a page load and 40 requests arrive in 200ms, then traffic is quiet.
variants.constraint: Short bursts are normal; sustained abuse is not.
variants.question: Which limiter shape fits?
variants.expectedPattern: Token bucket or leaky bucket that allows bursts but caps sustained rate.
wrongChoices: Hard 1 request per minute with no burst
A global mutex on all mobile traffic

variants.title: Expensive search endpoint
variants.context: Full-text search costs 50x a simple GET, and a few users monopolize the search cluster.
variants.constraint: Cheap endpoints should stay fast.
variants.question: How should limits differ?
variants.expectedPattern: Cost-based or endpoint-specific limits so expensive routes have a lower quota.
wrongChoices: The same QPS cap on health checks and search
No limit because search is important
Queue search inside the web thread with no cap

variants.title: Distributed counters disagree
variants.context: Each app instance counts locally and the true rate is 8x the intended limit.
variants.constraint: Instances do not share limiter state.
variants.question: What makes the limit correct?
variants.expectedPattern: A shared rate-limit store or a gateway that enforces the quota centrally.
wrongChoices: Limits only in the client SDK

variants.title: 429 with no Retry-After
variants.context: Clients retry immediately after 429 and the limiter never cools down.
variants.constraint: Honest clients will follow standard headers.
variants.question: What should the API return?
variants.expectedPattern: 429 plus Retry-After (or equivalent) so clients back off predictably.

variants.title: Partner SLA vs noisy neighbor
variants.context: A gold partner is starved because a free-tier integration shares one global QPS bucket.
variants.constraint: Tiers have different contracts.
variants.question: How should quotas be modeled?
variants.expectedPattern: Separate limit buckets per tenant and plan, not one global counter.
wrongChoices: One cluster-wide QPS for all keys
Unlimited gold traffic with no isolation

variants.title: GraphQL alias explosion
variants.context: A query uses 200 aliases to bypass a 100 req/min HTTP limit.
variants.constraint: HTTP QPS looks fine; resolver work does not.
variants.question: What must be limited?
variants.expectedPattern: Limit by query cost or resolver work, not only HTTP requests.
wrongChoices: Cache the attack query as a public object

variants.title: Webhooks retry us to death
variants.context: A partner retries failed webhooks at 100/s while we are already degraded.
variants.constraint: Inbound webhooks share the public edge.
variants.question: What stops the amplification?
variants.expectedPattern: Per-source webhook rate limits and a 429 that partners honor, plus a dedicated ingest path.
wrongChoices: Process every retry on the checkout thread

variants.title: Internal job stampedes the API
variants.context: A nightly backfill uses the public API without a quota and knocks over interactive traffic.
variants.constraint: The job is legitimate but unbounded.
variants.question: How do you isolate it?
variants.expectedPattern: A separate rate-limited (or internal) path with its own quota, not the interactive bucket.
wrongChoices: Run the backfill as anonymous public traffic
Give the job the admin cookie

variants.title: Clock skew on sliding windows
variants.context: Two gateways use local time for a 1-minute window and a client slips through both.
variants.constraint: Enforcement must be approximately correct globally.
variants.question: What keeps windows aligned?
variants.expectedPattern: A shared counter or synchronized window key, not independent local clocks as the only source of truth.
wrongChoices: Trust each node’s wall clock independently

variants.title: Limit on success hides failures
variants.context: Failed logins do not count toward the limit, so attackers iterate for free.
variants.constraint: Abuse is in the attempt, not the 200.
variants.question: What should increment the counter?
variants.expectedPattern: Count attempts (especially failures) on sensitive endpoints, not only successful calls.

variants.title: CDN caches 429 for everyone
variants.context: One user is limited and the CDN caches that 429 as a public response.
variants.constraint: Limits are per client.
variants.question: How should 429s be cached?
variants.expectedPattern: Do not share per-user 429s as public cache objects; vary by identity or skip cache.
wrongChoices: Cache 429 HTML for all users for 24 hours

variants.title: Websocket message flood
variants.context: HTTP is limited, but a socket sends 10,000 chat messages per second.
variants.constraint: The connection stays below HTTP QPS limits.
variants.question: Where else must limits apply?
variants.expectedPattern: Rate-limit messages per connection and per user on the socket path.
wrongChoices: Close sockets only after the database melts

variants.title: Fairness inside a bursty game server
variants.context: Matchmaking accepts all packets until CPU is 100%, then everyone times out.
variants.constraint: Need isolation before collapse.
variants.question: What is the first control?
variants.expectedPattern: Admit traffic only up to a safe rate and reject or delay the rest with a clear signal.
wrongChoices: Longer client timeouts as the only fix

variants.title: Shared NAT looks like one user
variants.context: A university NAT makes 4,000 students share one IP, so an IP limit blocks the campus.
variants.constraint: Abuse still exists, but IP is a coarse key.
variants.question: What identity should you prefer?
variants.expectedPattern: Limit by user or API key first; treat IP as a secondary signal.
wrongChoices: IP-only limits as the sole control

variants.title: Write amplification on comments
variants.context: Comment POST is cheap to receive but fans out to millions of notification writes.
variants.constraint: Ingress QPS understates real cost.
variants.question: How do you cap the damage?
variants.expectedPattern: Limit writes by user and by downstream fan-out cost, not raw POST count alone.
wrongChoices: Unlimited POSTs because bodies are small
Fan out synchronously with no cap
Disable notifications only after the queue is full

variants.title: Health checks counted as user traffic
variants.context: A load balancer probe hits / every second from 200 nodes and trips the global limiter.
variants.constraint: Probes must keep succeeding.
variants.question: How should probes be treated?
variants.expectedPattern: Exempt or separately bucket health checks so they do not consume user quota.
wrongChoices: Count probes as the noisiest tenant

variants.title: Soft limit then hard shed
variants.context: At 80% of quota the API still accepts work; at 100% it dies instead of degrading.
variants.constraint: Need a warning band before hard reject.
variants.question: What policy is missing?
variants.expectedPattern: Soft limits (slowdown or 429 with remaining budget) before hard shedding.

variants.title: Cron from every pod
variants.context: Each replica runs the same cron and 30 instances hit a partner API at 00:00.
variants.constraint: The partner’s rate limit is per account.
variants.question: What prevents the stampede?
variants.expectedPattern: Leader-elected or queued cron so only one producer runs, plus a client-side rate limiter.
wrongChoices: Every pod fires the same job
